Count.description: A whole number of things, never negative and at most 2^53 − 1, such as impressions, options, or a proposal's revisions, which its `version` counts.

Degrees.description: A geographic coordinate in signed decimal degrees, a latitude or a longitude, where the sign gives the hemisphere, as AdCOM 1.0 writes a `Geo`'s `lat` from −90.0 to +90.0 and its `lon` from −180.0 to +180.0. A receiver reads it as a number and never rounds it to a whole degree. The type states no bound, because the two bounds are the coordinate's and not the kind's, and one type carrying both would accept a latitude of 150.

Domain.description: A domain name, written as lowercase A-labels with at least two labels, a top-level label that starts with a letter, and no trailing dot, such as `examplepub.example`.

EpochMilliseconds.description: A point in time written as a whole number of milliseconds since the Unix epoch, `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`, as AdCOM 1.0 writes an `Ad`'s `init`, "Timestamp of the original instantiation of this ad … in Unix format (i.e., milliseconds since the epoch)". The unit is milliseconds and never seconds, so `1793664000000` is 2026-11-03 and the same instant written in seconds, `1793664000`, is a thousand times smaller and reads as 1970-01-21. The value is signed, because an instant before the epoch is a negative number of milliseconds, and it runs from −(2^53 − 1) to 2^53 − 1, the integers an I-JSON receiver reads exactly. A receiver compares two of them as instants, as it compares two Timestamps, and never adds them or reads one as a number of things.

Ext.description: An object for members the specification leaves to the parties to define, such as the Deals API's `ext` on each of its objects. It takes any members, and a receiver keeps the ones it doesn't know.

ExtendedDuration.description: A length of extended play in whole seconds, where `0` states that no extension is allowed and `-1` that an extension is allowed with no limit, as AdCOM 1.0 writes a `VideoPlacement`'s `maxext`. So the value is never below −1, and a receiver reads `-1` as "no limit" rather than as a length.

ExternalId.description: The identity of a record, a code, or a version that another system or list defines, such as a registry entry, a DSP seat, a geo code, a content category, a published document's version, or a field of the specification, named by its path as the specification's tables write it, carried as that system writes it. A receiver compares it by exact string equality and doesn't parse it; the field's description names where it comes from.

IntegerFlag.description: A yes or no written as an integer, `0` for no and `1` for yes, as AdCOM 1.0 and OpenRTB 2.6 write their flags, such as a placement's `instl`. A receiver reads it as a flag, never as a count, and a field that takes it keeps the integer its text writes.

Measure.description: What a metric that isn't a rate measures, a number never negative and not always whole, such as 1,200,000 audience impacts for DOOH or a modelled audience of 14.2 impacts per play.

MediaOffset.description: A point within a piece of media, in whole seconds from its start and never negative, such as the second of a video at which a mid-roll ad starts.

MinuteOffset.description: A local clock's offset from UTC in whole minutes, signed, where a negative value is west of UTC, as AdCOM 1.0 writes a `Geo`'s `utcoffset`, "local time as the number +/- of minutes from UTC". A receiver reads it beside a point in time and never as a length of time.

Text.description: Prose for people and agents to read. A receiver doesn't parse it or compare it.

VendorCode.description: A code that an AdCOM 1.0 list reserves for vendors, 500 or more, as List API Frameworks reserves "500+ Vendor-specific codes". It extends a vocabulary of the list's codes.
